task.title: Break a long formula into lines
task.shortdesc: A formula that is wider than its line breaks into lines at its operators. You choose the width, where the breaks go and how the lines are indented, or you choose another way to fit the formula.

context.p: CSSMedia breaks a formula, in a line of text or on a line of its own, at an mo or an mspace element that is a child of an mrow, of an mstyle, of the math element, or of another element that groups its children. It does not break inside a fraction, a root or a script. It puts on each line what fits, as a paragraph of text does. This formula has no break of its own, and it is 7 cm wide at most:

fig.title: A formula broken in a width of 7 cm

info.p: A formula is broken in the width of the box that holds it. The attribute maxwidth of math sets another width, a length. A formula file has no box, so maxwidth gives its width, and without it the file is not broken except where you force a break.

step.cmd: Choose another way to fit the formula

info.p: The attribute overflow of math says what happens to a formula that is wider than its width:

ul.li: linebreak, the default, breaks it into lines.
scale keeps it on one line and makes it smaller, so that it fits.
elide keeps it on one line and removes the middle of it. It keeps parts from the start and from the end, as many as fit, and puts an ellipsis between them.
truncate keeps it on one line and cuts it at the width.
scroll keeps it on one line. A PDF has no window to scroll in, so, as in a window that has not been scrolled, you see the start of the formula and the rest is cut at the width.

info.p: The attribute linebreak of mo and mspace says what a break there does:

ul.li: auto, the default, lets CSSMedia break there when the line is full.
newline always starts a new line there. On mspace, the value indentingnewline of MathML 3 is the same.
nobreak never breaks there, and not on either side of the element.
goodbreak prefers a break there, and badbreak avoids it, when the line is full and CSSMedia can choose between several places.

info.p: The attribute linebreakstyle of mo chooses where the operator goes when the line breaks at it: before puts it at the start of the next line, which is the default, after puts it at the end of the line, and duplicate puts it at both. The value infixlinebreakstyle takes what the attribute of that name says on mstyle or math. When a line breaks at an invisible times operator, the attribute linebreakmultchar is the character that is shown there, with the invisible times as the default.

fig.title: Forced breaks, and an operator at the end of a line

info.p: These attributes set where each line starts. On mo and mspace they apply to the lines after a break at that element. On mstyle and math they are the default for all the breaks inside. A percentage is a part of the width of the lines.

ul.li: indentalign aligns a line to the left, the center or the right, or to the position of another element with id. auto is the default, and it is the left.
indenttarget is the id of that element, which is in the same formula and on the line above. Without such an element, the alignment is auto.
indentshift is a length that moves the line from where indentalign puts it.

indentalignfirst and indentshiftfirst do the same for the first line of the formula. They are set on math, and they apply to a formula that has no break too. Their default is the value of indentalign and indentshift.
indentalignlast and indentshiftlast do the same for the last line, and for the second line of a formula that has two. Their default is the value of indentalign and indentshift.
lineleading is the space between lines, a length or a percentage of the normal height of a line, which is the default.
